text.p: These are the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- A meeting between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash was and is the aim of the United Nations, says U.N. envoy.
- Speculation intensifies that two deaths at psychiatric hospital were in fact murder.
- Council of Ministers to debate 1997 budgets today.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Police warn Turkish agents may try to stir up trouble following the killing of two Greek Cypriots in Dherinia last month.
- Irate Nicosia suburb residents hold protest next to site of monster disco.
- Left-wing party calls for talks with the Turkish Cypriot side without conditions.
- Dherinia killings will be centrepiece of president's speech to the U.N. General Assembly.
HARAVGHI
- Cyprus police are placed on alert after U.S. bombings in Iraq.
- More than 300 contract teachers in primary education have not yet been assigned to their posts, while schools open on Monday.
- Communist Akel party calls for an end to U.S. attacks on Iraq.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- The Dherinia murders have changed the scene for a solution. The U.S. and Britain are concerned at how a settlement can be implemented between the two sides.
- Cypriot authorities are concerned at possibility of murders of Turkish Cypriots by Turkish agents who will attempt to blame the Greek Cypriot side.
SIMERINI
- Rauf Denktash is putting pressure on Turkish Cypriots at the mixed community villages of Pyla and Potamia to settle in the occupied areas.
- Positions will open soon for five-year volunteers in the national guard.
